analysis.title: Morn note - Carl Hansen - 2026-11-03
key_insights: UBS downgrades adidas to Sell on slowing growth and margin pressure. UBSe 2027 sales growth is +4% vs consensus +7%, and gross margin is about 100bps below consensus. UBSe 2027-28 EBIT is more than 10% below consensus.
UBS cut adidas FY26-28 estimates by up to about 7%. The shares are up 20% from the early-October low, which UBS sees as a disconnect between valuation and the near-term earnings outlook.

UBS puts industry growth at low single digits in 2026 and 2027 vs a historical high single digit average. The adidas 2027 ambition of high single digit sales growth would need significant industry outperformance.

UBS downgrades Sonova to Neutral. Fundamentals are still constructive and UBS sees 2-5% underlying consensus estimate upgrades, but the shares are up 35% since July and trade at 24x PE, the highest-ever premium to EU Medtech.

UBS Evidence Lab survey of 303 largely independent US audiologists (fielded to 28 September) shows stable volumes, higher growth expectations for next year and pricing turning positive for the first time in over a year. Phonak ranks #1 on perception of new launches, with Oticon #2.
UBS stays Neutral on Sonova and Demant because share price outperformance suggests the hearing aid market improvement is largely understood by investors.

Nordic banks Q3 underlying pre-tax profit beat consensus by 3% on average. Jyske beat by 10% and Danske by 7%, driven by large loan loss reversals with much smaller beats at pre-provision profit level.
UBS expects Nordic banks to resume underperforming wider European banks. It attributes recent outperformance to risk-off positioning and does not see it as sustainable.

UBS defence report: NATO members agreed to lift defence and security-related spending to 5% of GDP by 2035, and Japan is doubling spending to 2% of GDP by FY2027. UBS identifies about US$259bn of potential funding for emerging defence capabilities to 2036, about 9% of 2025 global military expenditure.
UBS maps 144 companies with exposure to drones, counter-drone, electronic warfare, cyber, space and cloud, including 58 under UBS coverage.
UBS European Architect Business Survey Q3 2026 shows diffusion indices above 50 across all indicators, so activity is still growing, but the pace moderated vs the Q3 2025 survey.
Apple (Neutral) F4Q revenue was effectively in line with UBS estimates, with slightly better iPhone and Mac revenue. Services was in line, with headwinds in Search and the App Store.

Apple gross margin was 47.9%, capped by higher component costs and including an estimated 1 point benefit from a tariff refund. UBS sees gross margin risk and a material sequential slowdown in revenue growth over the next several quarters, which it expects to weigh on shares ahead of the call.

UBS Swiss Small & Midcap capex tracker: FY26E global capex growth expectations rose to 16% from 14% at 2Q26. FY27E is only marginally less strong, with support from previously weaker regions and sectors.

Logitech (Neutral in text) saw Europe sales down mid single digit on muted consumers, while North America was strong. Share was stable in Europe, so UBS attributes the weakness to the end market. Prime Day timing cost about 100bp, so Q2 FY27 sell-through would have been +2% y/y vs +1%.

Energy sector Q3 net income beat consensus by 7%, after consensus had been revised up 15% into the prints, driven by better refining. CFFO ex-WC beat by an average 10%, with OMV +28% and Shell +19%, while Eni was in line.
Puma (Neutral) Q3 top line was about 1ppt ahead of expectations. Inventory fell about 24% in Q3 and normalisation is expected to be complete by year-end. Shares rose about 6%.
UBS says Puma management's 2027 messaging shifted to a more gradual recovery. Visible Alpha consensus is about 4% growth vs UBSe about 3%, and the shares trade near 1.0x EV/sales.

Hugo Boss (Neutral) cut 2026 guidance on weaker consumer demand and higher non-cash expenses. It expects sales down high single digits and EBIT of €250-300m, about 11% below consensus and about 8% below UBSe at the midpoint.

The PBoC raised the FX deposit reserve requirement ratio from 4% to 6% effective November 15, after USDCNY strengthened nearly 1% since late September, including almost 100bp on Nov 2. The aim is to curb the pace of RMB appreciation.

Nordic banks Q3: underlying pre-tax profit beat consensus by 3% on average. Jyske beat by 10% and Danske by 7%, driven by large loan loss reversals, with smaller beats at pre-provision profit level.
Energy sector Q3: net income beat consensus by 7% after consensus was revised up 15% into the prints. CFFO ex-WC beat by 10% on average, with OMV +28%, Shell +19% and Eni in line.

Logitech FQ2 FY27: Europe sales fell mid single digit. Sell-through was +1% y/y, or about +2% adjusting for Prime Day timing. UBS expects Q3 FY27E sell-through flattish to low single digit growth excluding the semi incident.
Puma Q3: top line about 1ppt ahead of expectations, inventory down about 24%, shares up about 6%. Visible Alpha consensus for 2027 growth is about 4% vs UBSe about 3%.

Hugo Boss Q3 was better than expected, but 2026 guidance was cut. The company expects sales down high single digits (consensus and UBSe -8%) and EBIT of €250-300m, about 11% below consensus and about 8% below UBSe at the midpoint.
adidas: 2026 sales growth was about +10% (UBSe and consensus). UBSe 2027 sales growth is +4% vs consensus +7%, and 2027-28 EBIT is more than 10% below consensus.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong execution around the World Cup and a compelling apparel offering drove double-digit sales growth in 2026, and the shares recovered 20% from the early-October low.
tension_points.bear_case: UBS sees industry growth at low single digits and expects 2027 sales growth of +4% vs consensus +7%, with gross margin about 100bps below consensus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Meaningful acceleration in footwear and lifestyle growth, which UBS says it does not currently see.

tension_points.bull_case: A recovering US commercial hearing aid market and a new platform should drive 2-5% underlying consensus estimate upgrades.
tension_points.bear_case: Shares are up 35% since July and trade at 24x PE, the highest-ever premium to EU Medtech, so upgrades look priced in.

tension_points.bull_case: Inventory normalisation is expected to be complete by year-end and the top line came in about 1ppt ahead.
tension_points.bear_case: Management's 2027 messaging points to a gradual recovery, which may challenge consensus growth of about 4% vs UBSe about 3%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Clearer evidence that Puma's turnaround is gaining traction.
